ba-are-we-fast-yet[bot] opened issue #15210:

are-we-fast-yet found 4 regressions and 9 speedups in virtual cycles (callgrind) between Wasmtime 4182ebadb18e and 5619a5dab7b1.

  • Baseline: run 00091 (metadata), Wasmtime 4182ebadb18e
  • This run: run 00092 (metadata), Wasmtime 5619a5dab7b1

A change counts when a Mann-Whitney U test finds it significant at the 0.01 level and it clears its phase's minimum relative change:

compilation 0.3% 1%
instantiation 2.5% 20%
execution 0.5% 2%

A positive delta is a slowdown, a negative delta is a speedup.

instructions retired counts work done rather than how well it was predicted. A regression whose instructions didn't move is often Valgrind's branch predictors aliasing on a code layout change; see docs/regressions.md.

Each noise column is how far that event's own counts spread.

Commits

https://github.com/bytecodealliance/wasmtime/compare/4182ebadb18e5655c246a0e67e53b3213bcaa3cf...5619a5dab7b17c397d349570edf29373d1a7b279

  • 5619a5dab7b1 fix: Copying collector: grow-vs-collect heuristic compares against the w (#15207)
  • 0eccac5d55e8 cranelift: preserve rematerialization for cloned egraph values (#15205)
  • cfb483240b4d cranelift: handle interrupt_poll in inliner and emit stack map at faulting load PC (#14947)
  • 56ef38d8df37 cranelift: store Args/Rets pairs in Box<\[T\]> instead of Vec (#15197)
  • eb8f87349191 Keep inlined breakpoints when single-stepping ends (#15194)

Reproduce locally

On x86-64 Linux with Valgrind installed:

git clone https://github.com/bytecodealliance/sightglass
cd sightglass
git checkout 2d453335318d05cf42b6f3263aa68f0021985f10
rustc engines/wasmtime/build.rs -o build-engine
mkdir old new
REVISION=4182ebadb18e5655c246a0e67e53b3213bcaa3cf ./build-engine old
REVISION=5619a5dab7b17c397d349570edf29373d1a7b279 ./build-engine new
cargo run --release -- benchmark --measure callgrind \
  --engine old/libengine.so --engine new/libengine.so \
  --engine-flags-common="-Cparallel-compilation=n --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -Ccranelift-has-sse3 -Ccranelift-has-ssse3 -Ccranelift-has-sse41 -Ccranelift-has-sse42 -Ccranelift-has-popcnt -Ccranelift-has-avx -Ccranelift-has-avx2 -Ccranelift-has-fma -Ccranelift-has-bmi1 -Ccranelift-has-bmi2 -Ccranelift-has-lzcnt -Ccranelift-has-cmpxchg16b" \
  -- benchmarks/gcc-loops/benchmark.wasm benchmarks/kotlin-richards/kotlin-richards.wasm benchmarks/libsodium/libsodium-hash3.wasm benchmarks/libsodium/libsodium-keygen.wasm

alexcrichton commented on issue #15210:

My guess is #15207 is probably the 96% (!!) reduction in cycles and other improvements in GC benchmarks.

It then also seems that #15205 is likely the cause of the other execution slowdowns. cc @cfallin as this seems like it might be counter your expectations on #15205?

cfallin commented on issue #15210:

Hmm, interesting. The contributor on #15205 ran "real" benchmark timings (cycles) and these showed smaller impact than the Callgrind virtual cycle counts here; gcc-loops was the only >1-2% regression in the original timings (and the original timings saw some decent speedups too, overall fairly positive). I think I'll go with the real-machine-measured stats on this one...
